checks.question: Are trusted presentation, controlled UI and business ownership separate and public imports declared?
checks.detail: The trusted adapter consumes public ui component paths and injected resources/allocation; ui manifest has no plugin-framework dependency. Workbench owns persistence/provides; theme switching does not construct player/download/library instances. Repository package-boundary check passes. This is not a full UI or runtime dependency-graph audit.

checks.question: Are theme loaders build-known and failed loads retryable within the controller?
checks.detail: Only default/studio canonical descriptors are accepted, studio uses a literal dynamic import, and the controller does not retain a rejected custom loader promise. The supplemental import-rejection/retry scenario passes. This injected rejection test does not establish recovery from an actual browser module-fetch failure; directory/root graph acceptance stays pending.

checks.question: Are stale/disposed operations suppressed before entering the host allocation boundary, with resource release preserved?
checks.detail: B08-T01: the first generation/disposed check comes after prepareAllocation. A superseded studio import calls the allocation port after default has committed, and a resolved import calls it after dispose. Render snapshots still reject the old result; that does not suppress the callback. Existing and supplemental resource disposal/retry cases pass.

checks.question: Are theme preferences isolated and failures represented truthfully to the controlled selection UI?
checks.detail: Theme preferences store themeId and normalized per-theme settings independently from business snapshots. B08-T02: the same failure boolean covers persistence and activation, so a successful studio selection followed by a thrown write exposes a false default-fallback message.

findings.title: Check request freshness before invoking host theme allocation
findings.trigger: Start a delayed studio import, then commit default or dispose the controller before studio resolves.
findings.effect: The stale operation calls prepareAllocation(studio) before being rejected. The production callback awaits module readiness and calls host.controller.activate, so discarded renderer work can still initiate host activation/allocation. In the side-effectful port probe the rendered snapshot remains default while the port records studio after default. This proves the boundary call/order; a real host registry mismatch was not accepted or live-tested.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Recheck disposed/generation immediately after loading and before allocation; retain the post-allocation guard. Add permanent stale-load/disposal tests. Separately define cancellation/generation or side-effect-free staging for an allocation already in flight if the host boundary requires it; this audit does not claim a complete B05 host transaction review.

findings.title: Distinguish preference write failure from theme fallback
findings.trigger: Select studio successfully while runtime.storage.write throws for the new preference.
findings.effect: currentId() remains studio, but the controlled selection error says 界面主题不可用，已使用默认主题。可重新选择主题以重试。 The user is told a fallback occurred when only saving failed and receives no accurate persistence failure explanation.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Represent persistence/read/activation failure separately or derive feedback from the actual current state; keep the working theme usable and make saving retryable. Add a mounted composable regression that asserts both currentId and exposed error.
